objective: Evolve HYDRA into a general-purpose engineering agent competitive with AlphaCode, including provider compatibility
implemented: Bounded engineering agent loop with real file and process tools
Read-only mode and explicit command authorization
Workspace path guards and applicable AGENTS.md enforcement
Content-hash edit conflicts, atomic file writes and tracked diffs
Durable integrity-checked sessions, resume and conflict-aware rollback
Configured verification gate before completing code changes
Interactive follow-ups and CLI doctor
Full 60-entry upstream provider parity catalog with explicit statuses
51 provider transport profiles across compatible chat, Responses, Messages, Ollama, Azure and optional AWS Bedrock
Provider isolation, redirect refusal and provider-reported token accounting
Backward-compatible security workflow entry point
Opt-in unpacked Chromium extension with authenticated loopback bridge and explicit paired-tab origins
DOM snapshots, scoped interactions, screenshots and passive network metadata tools
Integrity-checked browser evidence, investigation hypotheses, alternative benign methods and snapshot comparisons
Unified engineering/security command router with legacy CLI and import compatibility
Session-local capability registry and separated file/process/session/browser handlers
Lazy configuration snapshots, initialization failure recovery and provider/security settings independence
Separated security lifecycle, workflow, result and console components
Separated confirmation evidence models, signatures and check groups with the existing SafeProber boundary
Loopback deployment defaults, explicit infrastructure passwords and Docker context exclusions
Interactive Textual engineering terminal with provider/model selection, durable sessions, plan/diff panels, live tool activity and asynchronous command approval

verification.bedrock_test: real SDK with Stubber; no AWS account request

remaining: Native subscription/OAuth integration for claude, auto-import, alphacode, openai, cursor, copilot, gemini, antigravity, google
Live provider/account validation with operator-configured credentials
Streaming native function calling and token/context budgets
General engineering delegation, broader browser QA and desktop tools
limitations: Approved commands have normal OS permissions and are not sandboxed
Rollback covers tracked file-tool changes, not arbitrary command side effects
Provider transport implementation does not establish live service availability or account access
AlphaCode feature parity and superiority are not claimed
